built: crossrefs.find(rows) is pure. It reads the references in each place of a file (library_service.source_rows rows) with a fixed pattern: subsection, paragraph or clause (x); lists and ranges ('(b) to (d)', 'sections 3 and 12'); section N; section N(x); § N(x); §§. 'subsection (a)' inside § 12 resolves to § 12(a), and 'section 3' to § 3 as a whole. A section carries over a page break. A place's own leading mark is never read as a reference, and a place referring to itself is not a link. A bare number followed by a time or unit word ('21 days') is not read as a section. A reference followed by 'of the <Name> Act' (or Regulations, Code, Law) is listed as pointing into another text and is not followed. 'of this Act' stays internal.

Each link holds: the source and target, the words as on the page with their line and offsets (lit), and a kind (EXCEPTION, CONSEQUENCE or REFERS) taken from fixed words. The kind is data only and is never said. The link also holds the desk's own quote of both ends and a sha256 of each end's words, with spaces as one.
A missing target is said plainly: '§ 12(c) refers to subsection (d), which is not in Demoland_Tenancy_Act.pdf.' (state MISSING).

Revisions are compared on read and nothing is stored, as with 0.8.6's pinned quotes. The earlier revision is the item of the same name in the same collection, with other bytes, whose latest ACCEPTED decision came before the current one's (by catalog_generation). Its places are cut from its own bytes by the reference extractor (document_extract.bounded, then library_service.source_rows) and cached in the process per (sha256, extractor hash). compare() gives each link a state. CURRENT: the same (source, target) wire existed and the words of both ends are unchanged; moving on the page does not count. RECHECK, with reasons NEW, FROM_CHANGED, TARGET_CHANGED or TARGET_NEW. MISSING: the target is not in the file. Wires the revision no longer has are listed as gone (NO_LONGER_REFERS or PLACE_GONE). With no earlier revision she says 'No earlier revision of X is on the desk, so there was nothing to compare.' If the earlier revision cannot be read she says 'cannot be read, so no link was compared with it.'
Kernel operation library.links {namespace, item?, label?}, read scope. It refreshes the Library's rebuildable index (library_service.refresh) and writes nothing else. No model (model_calls 0).

Ask the Library now adds up to 3 places of the same file that refer to the place it lit. The lit place is the model's checked hit or, with no model, the top place. Each is said as '§ 12(b) refers to § 12(a): “Subsection (a) does not apply if ...”' (crossrefs.into). The result also carries them as 'links'.

decisions_where_design_silent: Her line quotes the referring place word for word ('§ 12(b) refers to § 12(a): “...”'). The design shows a paraphrase ('§ 12(b) says (a) does not apply if no forwarding address was given in writing'). With no model the desk does not paraphrase, and a quote cannot misstate the text.

The earlier revision is found by the pinned-quote rule: the same file name in the same collection, admitted before the one admitted now. It is compared against its own bytes, on read. Nothing new is stored and no new record kind is added. One consequence: if an older revision is admitted again, it is compared with the revision just before it, so wires that differ go to recheck.

A wire is identified by (source label, target label). It stays CURRENT only while the words of both ends are unchanged, spaces normalised. Any change of words in either end, even outside the reference, sends it to recheck. A new wire also goes to recheck.

When a whole section is the target ('section 3'), it is compared using the words of all its places, joined. References into another named text are listed but not followed, and the desk is not searched for that text.
Nested marks such as (b)(i) are not modelled. places.split gives them flat labels, so 'paragraph (i)' resolves to § N(i), and when that place is not there it is said as missing.
